classification.difficultyReason: Translate the stake and net winnings into doubling and halving the current balance, then recognise that equal numbers of reciprocal multipliers cancel regardless of order.

content.prompt: Jim has $\$512$ and plays a game in which he has an equal chance of winning or losing. He wins four times and loses four times in random order. He bets half the money he has left at each stage. On a win, his stake is returned and he receives net winnings of twice his stake. On a loss, he loses his stake. How much does Jim have at the end?

answer.short:
$\$512$

Interpreting the payout as net winnings of twice the stake, each win doubles the balance and each loss halves it.
answer.worked:
Interpret “a win gives him twice what he bets” as net winnings of twice the stake, with the stake also returned. If his current balance is $M$, his stake is $\frac M2$.

$$\begin{align*}M_{\text{after a win}}&=M+2\left(\frac M2\right)\\M_{\text{after a win}}&=2M\\M_{\text{after a loss}}&=M-\frac M2\\M_{\text{after a loss}}&=\frac M2\end{align*}$$

Four wins and four losses therefore give:

$$\begin{align*}M_{\text{final}}&=512\times2^4\times\left(\frac12\right)^4\\M_{\text{final}}&=512.\end{align*}$$

The order does not matter because the same multipliers are multiplied together. Jim finishes with $\$512$.
